lessons.title: Farm disasters and how to prepare
lessons.html:
Farm disasters and how to prepare

A disaster is a sudden event that causes great damage or loss, such as a veld fire, flood, drought, hail storm or a serious disease outbreak. Farms cannot stop all disasters, but good preparation reduces losses and saves lives.

Common farm disasters in South Africa

  • Veld fires: especially in the dry winter months on the Highveld and in summer in the Western Cape. Strong wind spreads them fast.
  • Floods: after heavy rain, rivers rise and wash away soil, fences, crops and animals.
  • Drought: long periods without enough rain. Grazing and water run out.
  • Hail and storms: damage crops, orchards and buildings.
  • Disease outbreaks: such as foot-and-mouth disease or avian influenza, which can lead to quarantine and culling.
  • Pest outbreaks: such as locusts or fall armyworm.

Preparing for veld fires

  • Firebreaks are made and kept clear along boundaries and around buildings before the fire season. The National Veld and Forest Fire Act 101 of 1998 requires landowners to prepare and maintain firebreaks. Many farms belong to a Fire Protection Association.
  • Fire-fighting equipment (beaters, knapsack pumps, water tanks on a bakkie) must be ready and checked.
  • Workers must know the alarm signal, the meeting point and their role.

During a fire

  • Raise the alarm and tell your supervisor immediately. Call emergency services as the farm plan says.
  • Only trained workers fight fires, with the right PPE and in teams. Never fight a fire alone.
  • Never get between a fire and the wind direction; work from the burnt side.
  • Your life comes first. If the fire is out of control, move to safety.

Floods and storms

  • Never drive or walk through flooded rivers or low-water bridges.
  • Move animals and equipment to higher ground when warnings are given.
  • Shelter inside a strong building during lightning; stay away from fences, windmills and lone trees.

lessons.title: Conservation and recovery after disasters
lessons.html:
Conservation and recovery after disasters

Conservation means using natural resources wisely so they last. A farm with healthy soil, good veld cover and protected water sources suffers less damage in a disaster and recovers faster.

Conservation practices

ResourcePractice
SoilContour banks, planting across the slope, keeping crop residues and cover crops, repairing erosion gullies
VeldCorrect stocking rates, rotational grazing, resting camps, removing invasive alien plants
WaterProtecting river banks and wetlands, fixing leaks, not polluting water, using only the water the farm is allowed
WildlifeNot hunting without permits, protecting habitats, controlling problem animals legally

The Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983 requires farmers to protect soil, veld, water and wetlands and to control declared weeds and invader plants. The National Water Act 36 of 1998 protects water resources.

Drought management

  • Reduce animal numbers early, before the veld is overgrazed.
  • Keep fodder reserves and plan water supply.
  • Use water carefully; fix leaks and troughs.
  • Report animals losing condition.

After a disaster: supporting recovery

  1. Safety first: check for fallen power lines, damaged buildings and hot spots after fires before people go in.
  2. Care for animals: find and count them, give water and feed, and report injured animals to the supervisor and vet. Injured animals must not be left to suffer.
  3. Assess damage: record damage to crops, fences, pipes, buildings and machinery, with photos if possible. This is needed for insurance and government disaster relief.
  4. Repair priorities: water supply, fences to keep animals in, then other infrastructure.
  5. Protect the soil: burnt or flooded land is easily eroded. Keep animals off burnt veld until it recovers as the manager instructs, and repair gullies.

Your role

Know the farm's emergency plan, report hazards early, keep firebreaks and drains clear, and follow instructions during and after a disaster.

Key points

  • Disasters include veld fires, floods, drought, hail and disease outbreaks.
  • Prepare with firebreaks, equipment, an emergency plan and trained teams.
  • Never fight a fire alone or cross flooded rivers; your life comes first.
  • Conservation of soil, veld and water reduces disaster damage.
  • After a disaster: safety first, care for animals, record damage and protect the soil.

options.text: Keeping too many animals in one camp
